pr.title: Rename `UninhabitedEnumBranching` to `UnreachableEnumBranching`
pr.description:
Per [#120268](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/120268#discussion_r1517492060), I rename `UninhabitedEnumBranching` to `UnreachableEnumBranching` .

I solved some nits to add some comments.

I adjusted the workaround restrictions. This should be useful for `a <= b` and `if let Some/Ok(v)`. For enum with few variants, `early-tailduplication` should not cause compile time overhead.

r? RalfJung
pr.author: dianqk

classification.name: SimplifyCfg
evidence: shared implementation file: compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/simplify.rs; name present in diff

processing.reason: The PR is a rename plus a semantics-preserving optimization relaxation, not a bug fix, so there is no source-grounded incorrect transformation that changes observable values on concrete inputs. Reading the head implementation (compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/unreachable_enum_branching.rs) and the full diff confirms the only behavioral edit is in the `otherwise_is_last_variant` guard: old `!otherwise_is_empty_unreachable && allowed_variants.len() == 1 && check_successors(...)` becomes the same condition with `&& (targets.all_targets().len() <= 3 || check_successors(...))`. Both versions still require `allowed_variants.len() == 1` before retargeting the otherwise edge to the single remaining variant and making otherwise unreachable, and `allowed_variants.is_empty()` before making otherwise unreachable. When exactly one allowed variant remains, its discriminant is the only possible value reaching otherwise, so retargeting is sound; when none remain, otherwise is genuinely unreachable. Thus the relaxed cases execute identically, only producing better-optimized MIR. The two "errors" in the frozen analysis are either (1) hypothetical over-application by dropping the `len() == 1` invariant, which this PR does NOT do and which would be an unrelated manufactured rewrite, or (2) the old conservative guard, which is a missed optimization, not a value-semantics error. The historical tests are MIR-dump/codegen tests and do not demonstrate a concrete wrong value. Since the harness requires original and transformed executions to produce different defined values, no valid pair can be constructed from this PR without fabricating an ungrounded transformation, so I am not calling test_program_pair.

analysis.summary: Historical PR renames `UninhabitedEnumBranching` to `UnreachableEnumBranching`, clarifies that it eliminates branches on uninhabited *or* unreachable enum variants, and relaxes a CFG guard so small enums (at most 3 switch targets) are still rewritten despite the LLVM `early-tailduplication` concern. The core transform maps an `otherwise` edge to the sole remaining allowed variant and turns `otherwise` into an unreachable edge, but only when exactly one variant lacks a branch (or, separately, when no allowed variants remain and `otherwise` is not already empty-unreachable).
analysis.originalLogic: For a `SwitchInt` on an enum discriminant, the pass computes `allowed_variants` from the layout (uninhabited variants excluded) or, for generics, from `discriminant_ty.variant_range(tcx)`. It collects unreachable targets. It then decides `replace_otherwise_to_unreachable = otherwise_is_last_variant || (!otherwise_is_empty_unreachable && allowed_variants.is_empty())`, where `otherwise_is_last_variant = !otherwise_is_empty_unreachable && allowed_variants.len() == 1 && check_successors(...)`. When exactly one variant remains, the otherwise edge is retargeted to that variant's discriminant value and otherwise becomes unreachable; when no allowed variants remain, otherwise becomes unreachable. The pass runs only when `sess.mir_opt_level() > 0`, is placed after `RemoveZsts`/`RemoveUnneededDrops` and before `UnreachablePropagation` and `SimplifyCfg::AfterUnreachableEnumBranching`, and its old name/`SimplifyCfg` dump string were `uninhabited_enum_branching` / `SimplifyCfg-after-uninhabited-enum-branching`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Two distinct transformation errors must be separated. (1) Semantic over-application: converting the otherwise edge to `unreachable` or to an arbitrary variant when more than one allowed variant still has no explicit target. The invariant is that the otherwise edge may be replaced only when `allowed_variants.len() == 1`, because otherwise the default path can still be a valid inhabited variant (e.g. `Ordering::Less` vs `Greater`, or `Err`/`None` for `Option`/`Result`). (2) Historical optimization conservatism: before this PR the pass applied the `check_successors` guard unconditionally, so a small enum whose otherwise block had multiple successors was not rewritten even though the rewrite is valid; the PR bypasses the guard for `targets.all_targets().len() <= 3`, which is what enables `a <= b` and `if let Some/Ok(v)` patterns to optimize. Removing the guard entirely for large enums is the opposite mistake: it can expose `early-tailduplication` to complex switch CFGs, causing compile-time overhead and potential performance problems.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR functions containing `SwitchInt` terminators over enum discriminants, especially enums with custom discriminants, uninhabited variants, generic enums where only `variant_range` is available, and small enums such as `Ordering`, `Option`, and `Result`. Includes explicit `match` with a wildcard/otherwise arm, `a <= b`/ordering comparisons, and `if let Ok(x) = val` / `if let Some(v)`. The pass is relevant at optimization levels above zero, under both panic-abort and panic-unwind strategies. Custom-MIR tests are also in scope because they construct unusual switch target layouts with dead blocks.
analysis.trigger: A `SwitchInt` on an enum discriminant whose explicit targets do not cover all allowed variants. If exactly one allowed variant has no explicit target and the otherwise block is not already empty-unreachable, the otherwise edge is a candidate for retargeting to that variant and marking otherwise unreachable. If zero allowed variants remain and otherwise is not already empty-unreachable, otherwise is a candidate for becoming unreachable. For small enums, at most 3 switch targets, the otherwise-to-last-variant rewrite is attempted even when `check_successors` would reject it.
preconditions: The pass is enabled only when `sess.mir_opt_level() > 0`.
The discriminant must be recognizable by `get_discriminant_local`, which matches `TerminatorKind::SwitchInt { discr: Operand::Move(p), .. }`.
Allowed variants come either from enum layout `variant_discriminants` or, when layout is unavailable, from `discriminant_ty.variant_range(tcx)` with `discriminant_for_variant`.
The new small-enum bypass uses `targets.all_targets().len() <= 3`; larger switches still require `check_successors`.
The pass is ordered before `UnreachablePropagation` and before `SimplifyCfg::AfterUnreachableEnumBranching`, so dead-BB cleanup is observed in that later SimplifyCfg dump.
pitfalls: Do not treat every missing switch target as unreachable: a valid inhabited variant may remain as the default arm. Only rewrite otherwise when exactly one allowed variant remains (or none remain).
Do not retarget otherwise to an arbitrary variant; the code takes the single remaining variant after checking `allowed_variants.len() == 1`.

`check_successors` exists because of LLVM issue 78578 and `early-tailduplication`; the comment warns it 'causes compile time overhead and potential performance problems' when duplicating switch branches into predecessors. The small-enum exception is deliberately limited to at most 3 targets.
The parentheses change `|| (!otherwise_is_empty_unreachable && allowed_variants.is_empty())` only clarifies precedence; `&&` already binds tighter than `||`, so this is not a behavior change.

The PR is a rename plus optimization relaxation, not a confirmed bug fix. Old MIR test names and the old pass name remain in renamed diff headers; do not infer that the old pass was semantically wrong from retained names.
Panic strategy changes MIR dumps; tests use `EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_PANIC_STRATEGY` and separate `panic-abort`/`panic-unwind` expectation files.
Renaming the pass also renames the `SimplifyCfg` variant and dump string to `SimplifyCfg-after-unreachable-enum-branching`, so all `EMIT_MIR` and `//@ unit-test:` references must be updated together.
analysis.testStrategy: Use `tests/mir-opt/unreachable_enum_branching.rs` with `//@ unit-test: UnreachableEnumBranching`, `// EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_PANIC_STRATEGY`, and CHECK patterns asserting the resulting `switchInt` target mapping and the `otherwise` block's `unreachable;`. Cover `simple`, `custom_discriminant`, `otherwise_t1` through `otherwise_t5_unreachable_default`, and `byref`, including an otherwise arm that must remain a real fallthrough (`uninhabited_fallthrough_elimination.rs` keep/eliminate cases). Add codegen expectations in `tests/codegen/enum/unreachable_enum_default_branch.rs` for `implicit_match` (ordering/range case, with the comment that 'The otherwise branch must be `Less`') and `if_let` (expecting the 'same optimized code as a full match'). For the SimplifyCfg interaction, use custom MIR in `tests/mir-opt/simplify_dead_blocks.rs` with `//@ unit-test: SimplifyCfg-after-unreachable-enum-branching`, asserting that the dead constant-return block is gone and `switchInt` targets 0/255 at an unreachable block, 1 at a return block returning 2, and otherwise at the block returning `x` (the 'Check that we correctly cleaned up the dead BB' test).
evidence: //! A pass that eliminates branches on uninhabited or unreachable enum variants.
// Type instantiation may create uninhabited enums.
// Also eliminates some unreachable branches based on variants of enums.
// If and only if there is a variant that does not have a branch set,
// change the current of otherwise as the variant branch and set otherwise to unreachable.
// If there are some generics, we can still get the allowed variants.
// The main issue here is that `early-tailduplication` causes compile time overhead
// Despite the LLVM issue, we hope that small enum can still be transformed.
// This is valuable for both `a <= b` and `if let Some/Ok(v)`.
// We expect it to generate the same optimized code as a full match.
// Check that we correctly cleaned up the dead BB.
